key_insight: Model choice drives AI peer-review error detection most strongly, while verification tools provide task- and domain-specific gains.
engineering_relevance: Build scientific review assistants around strong base models, adding citation retrieval, computer algebra, and code execution where they provide measurable benefits.
method: Inject localisable errors across four types and three severity levels into real papers.
Measure detection by error type and severity, plus false positives on clean copies.
Evaluate Skepthical, a multi-agent reviewer using citation retrieval, computer algebra, and executed code.
evidence_signal: Across 30 astrophysics and ML preprints with 357 injected errors, 12 reviewer systems were evaluated; three frontier models using the same prompt differed by about 50 percentage points in total detection on both corpora.
watch_item: Tool gains are domain-dependent: Skepthical’s citation-detection lead in astrophysics did not extend to ML, and mathematics flags were the main source of false positives.
paper_title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
